transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Alicia Rivera (TideShore Head of ML), Tom Brenner (Infra Lead), Sara Lee (CTO)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick rundown — i'm maya, i'll be your AE, ravi is our solutions engineer. we want to lock down the POC scope: reserved gpus baseline, burst behavior, and the fallback policies.
[00:12] Alicia Rivera: yeah thanks, maya. we've been evaluating inference options. main ask is predictable latency for our summarization endpoints, and cost control — we need to understand reserved vs burst economics.
[00:25] Ravi Patel: great, can you remind us of target qps/latency and model size? that'll drive GPU sizing.
[00:30] Alicia Rivera: sure. production target is about 180 reqs/sec at peak for the summarizer (single-turn, ~700 tokens output). p95 latency target is <= 350ms, ideally 250ms. model is a 34B open model, we currently run it quantized to int8-ish on A100s.
[00:48] Tom Brenner: infra constraints — we run in a VPC, need KMS integration for keys and no public egress, and SOC-2 type logs for audit.
[00:56] Maya Chen: noted, we support VPC/private and KMS. for capacity — rough math, 34B quantized on an A100 gives about ~120-140 tok/sec depending on batch. for 700 tokens avg output and 180 req/s -> that's a lot of tokens. ravi, want to walk through the sizing calc?
[01:10] Ravi Patel: yeah. baseline approach: reserve capacity for sustained load, then allow burst into shared capacity. if we assume 700 tokens/output * 180 req/s = 126k tokens/sec. at say 120 tok/sec per GPU, naive division = about 1050 GPUs which is, obviously, not feasible. so we need to change the approach: larger batching, response chunking/streaming, prefix KV caching and model variant fallbacks.
[01:42] Alicia Rivera: whoa 1k gpus — ok that math helps. what levers we have? we are open to a smaller model for high concurrency or more aggressive quantization.
[01:50] Ravi Patel: levers: 1) batching — push to 16-32 tokens/batch where latency SLO allows; 2) KV/prefix caching for repeated prefixes — we saw up to 30% token reduction in prior workloads; 3) model variants — run a trimmed 8B for low-priority traffic, or a 34B-int8 with decoder-only kernel optimizations; 4) autoscale policy — reserved pool sized for base load (e.g., 60-70% of avg), burst into on-demand/dedicated shared pool for spikes, with automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model if burst can't supply capacity within N seconds.
[02:23] Sara Lee: fallback to smaller model — how does that impact fidelity? our product team will need to measure quality regressions.
[02:30] Ravi Patel: correct — part of the POC is quality monitoring and set of eval prompts. we'll push an eval harness to run side-by-side comparison and track key metrics (ROUGE/F1 and human review for a subset). fallback policy should be: primary model for first X attempts then fall to smaller if latency > threshold or queue depth high. we can tag responses with model_id so product can measure impact.
[02:52] Tom Brenner: network wise — if we burst to shared pool in our region, what's the cross-vpc connectivity and are we ok with data residency? also encryption at rest, audit logs.
[03:03] Maya Chen: for private we can keep control plane in your VPC; for hosted reserved, we support regional isolation and audit logs. we also support customer-managed KMS. i'll include the security doc.
[03:10] Alicia Rivera: good. on benchmarks — we'd like to run a representative 24-hour trace for baseline and then synthetic spikes (10x) for burst test. is that doable in a week?
[03:20] Ravi Patel: yes. POC plan we suggest: week 0 (artifact handoff), week 1 baseline sizing and reserved provisioning, week 2 burst benchmarks and autoscale tuning, week 3 integration + quality evals, week 4 wrap & go/no-go. kickoff benchmarks can be a 2-3 day concentrated run but we recommend a 24-72 hour baseline run to capture diurnal patterns.
[03:41] Alicia Rivera: timeline looks good. for reserved capacity sizing, any ballpark numbers given our targets after applying batching and KV caching?
[03:48] Ravi Patel: assume conservative improvements: batching + kernel opt -> 4x token throughput per GPU; KV caching -> 25% reduction in tokens; model variant -> route 20% low-critical to an 8B. Combined that could reduce effective tokens/sec by ~5x. so 126k tokens/sec / (120 tok/s * 4 * 0.75) ≈ 350 GPUs. still substantial, but now manageable with reserved pool plus burst and routing policy. if you can accept slightly higher p95 for low-prio traffic and route some requests to 8B, reserved could be ~120-150 GPUs with bursts to reach peak.
[04:24] Sara Lee: 120-150 reserved is within budget if costs align. can you provide cost estimates for reserved vs burst?
[04:31] Maya Chen: yes — we'll run a cost model in the proposal. typical pattern: reserved is cheaper per GPU-hour; burst uses on-demand pricing. we can also recommend quantization options that reduce GPU count further.
[04:41] Tom Brenner: autoscale specifics — what's the scale-up time? we care about how quickly the shared pool can pick up spikes.
[04:48] Ravi Patel: our autoscaler can attach burst instances in region within ~90-180s depending on capacity and warm caches. to mitigate, we use warm-provisioned buffer and fast-start cache warmers for common prefixes. plus fallback to a smaller model for immediate coverage under 10-30s.
[05:04] Alicia Rivera: fallback latency difference? users will notice. ideally the fallback is only for background or low-critical requests. can we tag request classes?
[05:13] Ravi Patel: yes, you can route by priority header. Redwood routing policy supports per-route SLOs and can enforce fallbacks only for routes labeled low-priority. high-priority always tries primary and will consume burst budget.
[05:24] Maya Chen: for the POC success criteria — let's confirm what you want us to measure: p95 latency <=350ms for high-priority, error rate <0.5%, cost/unit below X (you can specify target), and quality delta vs baseline model <Y for fallback paths.
[05:37] Alicia Rivera: we'll set cost/unit target after we see your cost model, but p95 350ms and error <0.5% are good. for quality delta, product wants <8% drop on summarization metrics when using fallback for <20% of traffic.
[05:47] Ravi Patel: noted. we'll instrument evals and tag responses. we'll also provide telemetry hooks for your observability (Prometheus traces, per-token cost breakdown).
[05:58] Tom Brenner: for the security review — we need SOC2 compliance evidence and network architecture diagram for the private deployment.
[06:05] Maya Chen: i'll attach SOC2 summary and_arch, and we'll schedule a security deep-dive with our compliance engineer if needed.
[06:12] Alicia Rivera: okay let's talk data — will any request payloads leave our VPC if we do private?
[06:18] Ravi Patel: in Private mode customer data can stay inside your network and we can run inference on-prem or in your VPC; for hosted reserved there is cross-network traffic but it's regionally isolated. we'll outline options in the doc.
[06:28] Sara Lee: what about KV cache consistency? if we have many replicas, cache hit rate is important for performance.
[06:33] Ravi Patel: our runtime uses a distributed KV cache with per-pod local caches and eventual consistency for noncritical prefix caching. we'll show observed cache hit rates from previous pilots (we typically see 20-40% hit on chat-like workloads). caching config will be part of tuning in week 2.
[06:48] Maya Chen: ok, next — benchmarks: ravi can share the harness and recommended configs. you'll provide traces and model artifact; we run a baseline and then spike tests with 5x and 10x traffic. we do both latency SLO tests and long tail run for 24-72h.
[07:03] Ravi Patel: i will share a runnable container with the harness and a README of env vars. it includes: request replayer, payload anonymizer, shaper for spike patterns, and a script to capture per-token timings.
[07:12] Alicia Rivera: we will need a walkthrough on the harness. can we do the benchmark kickoff with your SEs involved?
[07:16] Maya Chen: yes — let's set a 60-minute kickoff the week of 7/27.
[07:20] Tom Brenner: one more infra question — are warm caches saved across scale-down/up events or do we hit cold start penalties?
[07:25] Ravi Patel: we support warm snapshots of KV for quicker warmup; we also have pre-warmed instances (buffer pool) that maintain KV shards. those are optional — part of the POC config we can enable a small warm buffer to lower cold-start tail.
[07:37] Alicia Rivera: great. anything else on the fallback policy? we want to be explicit on how routing decisions made.
[07:42] Ravi Patel: fallback policy proposal: 1) soft-queue threshold (requests longer than 3s) -> route to fallback model; 2) autoscale cooldown 120s to avoid thrashing; 3) percentage-based fallback for low-priority routes (e.g., 0-20% sampling for quality monitoring), 4) tagged responses for audit. we'll include a yaml example in the config.
[08:03] Sara Lee: will the POC include canary rollouts for model updates?
[08:07] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood supports canary/A-B rollouts. we can test one model version vs another during the POC.
[08:13] Alicia Rivera: ok let's summarize and confirm owners.
[08:17] Maya Chen: recap: artifacts due 7/24 — customer provides traces and model; redwood provides POC proposal + cost model by 7/24; ravi shares harness + config; benchmark kickoff week of 7/27; POC runs 4 weeks with baseline, burst, quality evals; final go/no-go end of week 4.
[08:33] Tom Brenner: sounds good. also need security deep-dive — can we tentatively book that for the second week?
[08:39] Maya Chen: yes, we'll propose dates when i send the security pack.
[08:42] Alicia Rivera: thanks everyone — excited to see the numbers.
[08:46] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with the proposal and links.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heards — 'K-V cash' sometimes typed instead of 'KV cache', 'sock two' for SOC2, 'A100s' sometimes 'A tens' in raw transcript. speakers labeled by name but some segments auto-labeled 'Speaker 2' in original export — cleaned minimally for readability.
